title: Prompt Compactors Journal
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad to evolve compact prompt templates and a small curated few-shot set that minimize token cost while preserving instruction-following and reducing hallucination. Not a final library entry — working notes, heuristics, and failure taxonomy.

Context + constraints:
- Target use: low-latency mobile assistant endpoint with aggressive token budget (<= 180 tokens input + expected response).
- Models: evaluating on two families: rwd-medium-16k (quantized) and community-llama-2-13b (float). Behavior diverges on succinct instructions and truncated context.
- Eval harness: abbreviated tests (A/B) with 120 sample prompts across 6 intents (qa, summarization, rewrite, code-small, persona-chat, extraction).

Design goals (ranked):
1) Preserve instruction specificity (no ambiguous pronouns).
2) Avoid superfluous examples that increase cost without improving scores.
3) Make fallback micro-prompts for partial contexts.

Experiment ideas (to run this week):
- Progressive compaction: start with long canonical template, remove/merge sentences until performance drop >3% instruction-following. Log token_delta vs metric.
- Phase-shift few-shot: move exemplar ordering from exemplar-heavy to exemplar-minimal + one negative example to see contrastive effect on hallucination.
- Prefix anchoring vs slot anchoring: compare "You are an assistant that X." vs embedding role inside bracketed slot [ROLE: assistant-with-constraints].

Template skeleton (compact-first approach):
- Compact prompt (version C1):
  System: "You are a concise assistant. Prioritize correctness and brevity. If unsure, say 'I don't know'."
  Instruction: "{task}. Use only the facts provided. Output must be a short JSON with keys: answer, sources (list)."
  Context: "{context}"
  Shots: 1 minimal positive example when needed (see shots section).
  Post: "MaxTokens: 120; Tone: neutral; No additional commentary."

- Verbose prompt (v0) kept for control runs.

Few-shot set sketches (contrastive compact set):
- Shot A (positive):
  Q: "What is the capital of Greenland?"
  A: "answer: Nuuk; sources: [Wikipedia]"
- Shot B (negative/contrastive):
  Q: "Is Greenland an independent country?"
  A: "answer: No; explanation: It is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark; sources: [CIA World Factbook]"
- Rationale: one positive, one contrastive to force narrow output shape and discourage confident hallucination. Keep examples token-efficient (3–6 tokens extra per example).

Failure buckets observed so far (taxonomy draft):
- Hallucinated-fact: model invents entities not in context. Trigger: metaphor-rich prompts or vague questions.
- Overconfident-incomplete: model gives partial answer without signaling uncertainty.
- Repetition-bloat: model repeats context phrases when prompt asks to summarize -> bloated tokens.
- Slot-misplacement: when asked to output structured JSON, model emits plain text or wrong keys.
- Instruction-drift: model obeys tone but fails task (e.g., rewrites instead of summarizing).

Quick mitigation heuristics matched to buckets:
- Hallucinated-fact: add explicit "Only use facts present in the context or say 'I don't know'" and add one negative contrastive shot.
- Overconfident-incomplete: enforce "If answer incomplete, return partial_answer: true and a reasoning_hint field."
- Repetition-bloat: add token cap enforcement note in system and request bullet-list output with max 3 bullets.
- Slot-misplacement: include exact JSON schema as an example and a one-line aligner: "Return strictly valid JSON with keys X,Y."

Micro-experiments log (short):
- 2024-02-21: ran compact C1 vs verbose v0 on 40 QA prompts. C1 token-savings: ~22% median. Instruction-following delta: -1.2% (acceptable). Hallucination down 0.6% (surprising).
- 2024-03-04: added negative contrastive shot -> hallucination dropped another 1.5% but some extraction tasks lost specificity.
- 2024-04-01: tried prefix anchoring -> marginally better on rwd-medium, worse on community-llama-2-13b. Suggest model-specific template variant mapping.

Evaluation metrics to capture per run (keep CSV-friendly):
- tokens_input, tokens_output, instr_follow_score (0-1), halluc_rate (0-1), json_valid_rate (0-1), latency_p50_ms, cost_estimate ($).

Quick TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Build small script to auto-trim template until instr_follow_score < threshold (linear search). Ticket: LINEAR-2381.
- [ ] Add gating for model-specific template mapping (config + default fallback).
- [ ] Curate 12 more compact contrastive shots for extraction tasks.
- [ ] Run 1k prompt sweep on weekend via cheap batch infra (ephemeral).
- [ ] Document common failure examples with raw model outputs for debugging (store in /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/prompt-registry/examples).

Notes to self (loose):
- Try micro-format: single-line examples inside triple-quoted blocks may preserve structure better in streaming.
- Watch out for token counting mismatches with different tokenizers; run tokenization step locally for each model variant.
- Consider a tiny verifier: after model outputs JSON, run a quick parse/validate step and if invalid, re-prompt with strict schema enforcement (2nd chance).

Questions / open hypotheses:
- Does the negative contrastive shot help more for generative QA than for structured extraction? My quick runs say yes for generative QA. Need systematic split analysis.
- Is there an optimal exemplar length (characters) given quantized models tend to truncate KV cache sooner? Hypothesis: shorter examples win for quantized.

Snippets to paste into eval harness (quick copy):
- System line: "You are a concise, cautious assistant. If uncertain, say: 'I don't know'. Keep answers short and provide sources when possible"
- Compact instruction template: "{task}. Use context. Output JSON: {\"answer\": string, \"sources\": [string], \"confidence\": low|med|high}."

Changelog (brief):
- 2024-02-19 initial notes 
- 2024-02-21 first compact vs verbose run
- 2024-03-04 added contrastive negative shots
- 2024-04-01 model-anchoring experiments
- 2024-06-03 cleaned and moved TODOs to linear

End-of-file: keep this doc light. When ready, will convert top experiments into a proper PR under prompt-registry and a small confluence draft for the team.
